title: Relative dynamic attracting subgroup and its positive tangent weights
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over this base. Put $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units and $\mathbf G_{a,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[x]$ with addition. For a smooth group $H/S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], write $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\ker(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A))$, with addition from multiplication and scalar action from $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. Let $H/S$ be smooth affine of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], equipped with an action $a:\mathbf G_{m,S}\times_SH\to H$ by group automorphisms. For each $A$-algebra $B$ define $U_a(B)$ to consist of those $h\in H(B)$ whose orbit map $t\mapsto a(t,h)$ extends from $\operatorname{Spec}B[t,t^{-1}]$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ with value $1_H$ at $t=0$. This extension is unique. The functor $U_a$ is represented by a smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup of $H$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with geometrically connected unipotent fibres; unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. If $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}\mathfrak h_j$ is the coaction weight decomposition for $a$, then
$$\operatorname{Lie}(U_a)=\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathfrak h_j\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(H).$$
The action preserves $U_a$ and all its points have the above contraction within $U_a$ itself. If $H'$ is another smooth affine finitely presented group with such an action $a'$ and $f:H'\to H$ is an equivariant $S$-group homomorphism, then $f$ carries $U_{a'}$ into $U_a$. Formation of these subgroups, their tangent inclusions and these induced maps commutes with arbitrary and successive ring base changes. Geometric connectedness means connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme] after extension to an algebraic closure of each residue field. Neither reductivity nor connectedness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 4.1.7(1),(2),(4), printed pp.112-114, and Proposition 4.1.10(2), printed p.115 (equivariant functoriality); arbitrary base change noted before that proposition. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative algebraic-group theorem.

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$. Two extensions of the same orbit give algebra maps $C\to B[t]$ whose composites with $B[t]\hookrightarrow B[t,t^{-1}]$ agree. This inclusion is injective over every ring $B$, by uniqueness of Laurent coefficients, so the extensions agree. This proves uniqueness without reducedness or a field hypothesis.

source.place: Conrad, before Definition 4.1.6, printed pp.111-112; affine coordinate argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] with $R=A$, $G=H$ and the given action. Its hypotheses are exactly smoothness, affineness and finite presentation, all assumed here. Its functor $U_a(B)$ is the present functor, including over nonreduced test algebras. It therefore represents it by a smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup with geometrically connected unipotent fibres, and identifies its tangent inclusion with $\bigoplus_{j>0}\mathfrak h_j$. That node also gives arbitrary and successive base change of this subgroup and tangent identification. No connectedness of $H$ or reductivity is used.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem 4.1.7(1),(2),(4), printed pp.112-114; reuse of the existing more general relative theorem.

proof.text: Use the coordinate description in [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups]. Write $C=\bigoplus C_n$, let $\epsilon:C\to A$ be identity evaluation and let $I$ be generated by $C_n$ for $n<0$ and $f-\epsilon(f)$ for $f\in C_0$. This ideal is homogeneous, so $D=C/I$ is nonnegatively graded with $D_0=A$; the counit kills nonzero degrees because the identity is fixed, so it splits the structural map $A\to D$. The formula $\bar f_n\mapsto s^n\bar f_n$ for $n\geq0$ defines an algebra map $D\to D[s]$. It gives a morphism $\mathbf A^1_A\times U_a\to U_a$ restricting to the original action on units, equal to the identity at $s=1$, and equal to the identity section at $s=0$. Thus the action preserves $U_a$, and the contraction of every point occurs inside $U_a$ itself.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem 4.1.7 proof, printed p.113, coordinate ideals; agent expansion of the contraction.

proof.text: For an equivariant group homomorphism $f:H'\to H$ and $u\in U_{a'}(B)$, compose its extended orbit $\gamma_u:\mathbf A^1_B\to H'_B$ with $f_B$. On units this is the orbit of $f_B(u)$, and at zero its value is $f_B(1)=1$. Hence $f_B(u)\in U_a(B)$, naturally in $B$, defining the required restricted morphism. For any $A\to A'$ and any $A'$-algebra $B$, the test point, extended orbit and composition are the same maps whether considered over $A$ or $A'$. Under the base-change identifications in [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups], the induced morphisms therefore agree. Their derivatives agree by evaluating on $B[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and taking kernels of reduction. Repeating for $A\to A'\to A''$ gives the same maps and tangent inclusions, proving successive compatibility as well.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 4.1.10(2), printed p.115, functoriality; paragraph before the proposition, printed p.114, base change; agent expansion via test algebras.

Base item (side-live): unsplit, no proof, so this is not a re-split. Statement correction: 'equivariant' became 'equivariant S-group homomorphism'. The counterexample holds: x↦x+1 on G_a with the trivial action is equivariant but moves U_a={0}. Conrad 4.1.10(2) is stated for homomorphisms. The only citer, lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential, applies it only to the group homomorphism V_α→G, so no citer breaks. Step 1: uniqueness follows because B[t]→B[t,t^-1] is injective; elementary. Step 2: cites the existing unsplit lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups (Q56, same unit, proof_deps empty, so no cycle). Its hypotheses match exactly (smooth affine fp, action by group automorphisms) and its U_a is the same functor. It gives representability, connected unipotent geometric fibres, Lie(U_a)=⊕_{n>0}g_n and arbitrary/successive base change. Step 3: from its coordinate ideal (C_{<0}, f-ε(f)), I checked that the ideal is homogeneous, that ε(C_n)=0 for n≠0 so D_0=A, and that f_n↦s^n f_n is a ring map equal to the identity at s=1 and the identity section at s=0; the action preserves U_a. Step 4: f∘γ_u is the orbit of f(u) with value f(1)=1 at 0; Yoneda gives the map; base change and tangent compatibility hold because the maps are literally the same. Small cases checked: trivial action, G_a with weight n>0, weight ≤0, finite étale H, A=0. Conrad is not available locally and is correctly listed as WANTED, so page numbers were not verified.
